question: What is the dark layer that develops on silver upon its corrosion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Silver sulphide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The dark or black layer that develops on **Silver** articles when exposed to air for a long time is **Silver sulphide**.
 
• This chemical process is specifically known as **Tarnishing**. It occurs because **Silver** reacts with **Hydrogen Sulphide (H2S)** gas present in the **Atmosphere**.
 
• The chemical formula for the black coating formed is **Ag2S**. Unlike the corrosion of iron, **Silver sulphide** is relatively stable and forms a thin film that protects the underlying metal from further deep **Corrosion**, although it ruins the luster.
 
• The reaction can be summarized as: **Silver (Ag)** reacting with **Sulphur compounds** and **Oxygen** to produce **Silver sulphide** and water/hydrogen.
 
• This layer is highly insoluble in most solvents and requires specific chemical treatments, such as Electrochemical red
